reliable_uses: Define a deterministic Step 1 model that turns deck research into machine-readable pre-run artifacts without claiming runtime proof or gameplay correctness.
Compile source-backed mulligan anchors into runtime-safe Mulligan.json rows and keep unsupported conditional logic in suppression reports instead of emitting risky runtime rules.
Compile per-card role, timing, target, discover, choose-one, and hero-power intent into per-card CARDID.json files whose GameCardId matches the filename stem.
Translate only concrete ordered combo sequences into Combo.json, while keeping symbolic or unresolved combo ideas in contract or suppression artifacts.
Materialize GlobalValues.json from the live runtime default baseline and limit pre-run policy to explicit board-value or turn-weight assumptions that are documented in the gameplan contract.

Use deck_research_contract.json, gameplan_contract.json, card_obligation_matrix.json, and decision_trace_requirements.json as the control plane that separates source-backed assumptions from later runtime evidence.
Use HearthstoneJSON card metadata, HSReplay mulligan filters, and current deck-guide or meta sources as upstream research inputs for card IDs, curve tags, matchup priors, and opening-hand anchors.
Fail closed on unsupported or weakly specified surfaces so the first generated package is conservative, reviewable, and acceptance-gated rather than over-automated.
limitations: Official HearthRanger pages define syntax and documented semantics, but they do not prove that a generated package loads correctly in the live runtime or improves gameplay.
Community guide and data sources such as HSReplay and Vicious Syndicate are useful for priors, but they are meta-dependent and should not alone authorize runtime writes or broad tuning.
Static deck research cannot prove CONFIG_LOAD_OK, RUNTIME_SAMPLED, FINETUNE_READY, gameplay improvement, or patch correctness; those remain post-run evidence claims only.

Symbolic combo ideas, hidden-information lines, random or discover outcomes, transformed hero-power identity, and unresolved generated-token lineage cannot be treated as strict deterministic config facts before runtime evidence exists.
The current local runtime package treats Concede.json and Presume.json as registry-known but unsupported runtime surfaces, so they should not be part of default HSConfig generation today.
GlobalValues is a broad board-value control surface; a single speculative change can affect many decisions, so it is a poor first target for aggressive automatic tuning.

Mulligan condition expressiveness is intentionally narrower than the full documented JSON grammar in the current runtime-safe pipeline, so some source-backed matchup logic will need suppression or review instead of emission.
A valid syntax preview is still not a full syntax-registry proof because the local model is conservative and does not exhaustively machine-check every documented keyword and version gate.
architectural_implications: HSConfig should generate contracts first, then compile runtime files from those contracts; direct free-form generation into runtime JSON should be avoided.

The deterministic decision model should be layered as research intake -> research contract -> gameplan contract -> config surface compilers -> preview validation -> guarded runtime write -> acceptance gate.

Mulligan generation should use a dedicated mulligan compiler that converts source-backed anchors into documented hold or discard rows, preserves ordering semantics, and suppresses non-runtime-safe expressions into a separate report.
Card behavior generation should target per-card CARDID.json files only, because aggregate CardBehavior.json is not a supported runtime package surface in the current local contract.

Target and use rules should be represented in gameplan semantics first as card_usage, target_policy, hold_policy, forbidden_actions, and related clauses, then lowered into CARDID.json rule blocks only when the mapping is explicit.

Combo generation should require concrete ordered card ID chains and explicit role labels such as setup, payoff, or protection; symbolic sequences should remain visible in combo suppression or review artifacts rather than being emitted.

GlobalValues generation should be baseline-first: copy the full live default file, profile all keys, and allow only narrow documented overlays such as turn-weight assumptions before any fresh games are played.

Presume and Concede should stay outside the default compile path until HSConfig intentionally adds first-class authoring, validation, and patchability support for them; until then they should be treated as documented but disabled surfaces.
Every emitted row should carry provenance back to a gameplan clause, source document key, and confidence marker so later Step 2 review can explain why a runtime rule exists.

Validation should distinguish deterministic pre-run readiness from runtime proof: a package may be READY_FOR_USER_RUN while still being blocked from any claim about config load, optimal play, or gameplay improvement.
Assuming the bot plays optimally is acceptable only as a Step 1 prior for initial artifact generation; it is not a license to infer missing runtime evidence or to skip read-only Step 2 analysis.
recommended_contracts: deck_research_contract.json as the normalized static evidence bundle that records card roles, card usage expectations, source refs, contract quality, and explicit gaps.

gameplan_contract.json as the semantic source of truth for mulligan_plan, correct_play_semantics.card_usage, target_policy, resource_policy, hero_power_policy, combo_sequencing, unknowns, and global_values_contract.
mulligan_anchor_map.json as an upstream research artifact that stores default keeps, matchup keeps, coin or no-coin branches, and rationale before runtime-safe down-compilation.

card_target_use_contract.json as a machine-readable intermediate that resolves each deck card into use window, hold policy, target owner rules, discover or choose-one policy, and forbidden actions before file emission.
combo_sequence_contract.json as an intermediate that stores ordered card ID chains, same-turn versus cross-turn separators, role labels, and exact emission eligibility.
global_values_policy_contract.json as a narrow contract that records baseline source hash, allowed overlay keys, board-value intent, turn-weight assumptions, expected effect, and rollback posture.

config_row_provenance.json as a one-row-per-generated-rule matrix linking each emitted Mulligan, CARDID, Combo, or GlobalValues row to rule_id, source_doc_key, source_gameplan_key, confidence, and patchability class.
supported_surface_registry.json as a checked registry that separates documented syntax surfaces from locally supported runtime-package surfaces.
config_generation_decision_report.json as a compact compiler output that lists emitted files, suppressed rows, blocking reasons, and acceptance-relevant evidence.
never_autogenerate_without: Exact deck identity inputs: deck name, deck code, resolved card list, and concrete card IDs from a reliable card-data source.
A validated deck_research_contract.json with source-backed card_role_map and card_usage_expectations rather than generic fallback knowledge only.
A validated gameplan_contract.json that covers mulligan semantics, card usage, target policy, hero power policy, resource policy, combo sequencing, unknowns, and global_values_contract.
A current VisionAI syntax source stamp or manifest reference for the documented surfaces being emitted.
Runtime default GlobalValues baseline access plus a full key profile so GlobalValues.json is copied from the real baseline rather than invented from a reduced shape.
Per-row provenance coverage for every generated runtime rule so each row is traceable to a contract clause and source reference.
Runtime-safe compiler outcomes for Mulligan and Combo, including suppression reports for any source-backed logic that cannot be emitted safely.
Strict preview validation for file shape, GameCardId routing, supported surface checks, combo parity, and GlobalValues values-block structure.
A fake runtime receipt, same-invocation runtime surface snapshot, and acceptance_report.json that reaches READY_FOR_USER_RUN before any live package handoff.
Fresh post-run evidence before any claim about config load, optimal play, strict patch promotion, or post-Step-1 tuning.
